NDT training in Denver: how it works for Denver employers and technicians

NDT training for Denver and Front Range employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. The employer issues certification under its written practice once classroom training, on-the-job experience, examinations and an annual vision test are complete.

The overview above explains the two NDT economies on the Front Range, aerospace and energy, and why their qualifications do not transfer. This section goes further for the people who actually have to make training happen: technicians in Commerce City, Brighton, Greeley and Aurora, and inspection and fabrication managers trying to certify crews spread across a long stretch of I-25. It covers what each method course includes, the certification path, how onsite delivery works in Colorado conditions, the regulators that matter, and a Denver FAQ.

Atlantis does not have a Denver classroom. Theory is delivered live online, which suits a workforce that may be in Weld County one day and Pueblo the next, and practical training happens at your facility on your own equipment.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Denver

MethodLevelsWhat Denver employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, IIIWall thickness on DJ Basin gathering lines and facility piping, refinery corrosion monitoring, structural weld inspectionLevel I: none beyond the written practice. Level II: UT Level I plus experience
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, IIIPipeline girth welds, corrosion mapping, heavy fabrication weldsNormally UT Level II
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, IIIWeld flaw sizing on thick pressure equipment and power plant componentsNormally UT Level II
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, IIIPipeline and facility welds, castings, industrial component radiographyRadiation safety training and Colorado radiographer requirements; RT Level I before Level II
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, IIIStructural steel, oilfield equipment and tubulars, rail and heavy equipment componentsLevel I: none. Level II: MT Level I plus experience
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, IIINon-ferrous and stainless components, aerospace supplier parts, stainless process weldsLevel I: none. Level II: PT Level I plus experience
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, IIIPipeline and facility construction, structural steel, bridges, tank inspectionsLevel I: none; usually first
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, IIIHeat exchanger tubes at power and process plants, surface cracking on aircraft and componentsLevel I: none. Level II: ET Level I plus experience

Ultrasonic Testing. UT content runs from wave physics, velocity and attenuation through calibration, thickness gauging and angle-beam weld examination. For Front Range energy work we emphasise thickness surveys on production and gathering piping, erosion at elbows and tees, and readings on cold steel, because winter field work changes coupling and velocity behaviour. Level II students write technique sheets, evaluate indications and report to the governing code.

Phased Array and TOFD. Open to UT Level II technicians. PAUT covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scanning, encoded data and scan-plan coverage; TOFD covers diffraction theory, probe spacing, dead zones and sizing. In Colorado, demand comes from pipeline construction contractors, heavy fabricators and power generation.

Radiographic Testing. RT covers physics, exposure calculation, geometry, image quality, film and digital technique and interpretation of weld and casting images. The course explains where your NDT certification ends and Colorado's radiation licensing begins.

Magnetic Particle and Penetrant: cold-weather reality. This is where Denver differs from Gulf Coast training. Penetrant testing to ASME Section V has a standard temperature range, and below it you need a procedure qualified for the lower temperature. On a January morning on the plains east of Denver, steel can be well below that range. Our PT course teaches technicians to measure part temperature, recognise when the standard technique is invalid and escalate to a qualified procedure rather than improvise. MT covers yoke and prod technique, field indicators, lift tests, fluorescent inspection and interpretation on oilfield and structural components.

Visual Testing. VT covers direct and remote technique, lighting (including glare and bright high-altitude sun, which is a real issue outdoors), weld gauges, corrosion measurement and documentation.

Eddy Current Testing. ET covers induction, impedance-plane analysis, probe types and frequency selection, with applications in exchanger tubing during outages and surface-crack detection on components.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Denver, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. The foundation. It sets training, experience, examinations, vision testing and recertification by method and level.
  2. Classroom training to the written practice minimums. Rather than repeat hour figures here, see the method-by-method table in our training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience, logged and supervised. Field technicians should record the job, method and time for every day of NDT work.
  4. General exam on principles and theory.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's equipment, procedures and codes, such as API 1104 for pipelines or AWS D1.1 for structural steel.
  6. Practical exam on flawed specimens, administered or overseen by the designated Level III.
  7. Vision test, near-vision and colour-contrast, annually.
  8. Employer certification, signed by the Level III and employer.
  9. Recertification on the interval in the written practice.

More detail is in our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Denver crews

  • Live online classroom for technicians spread from Fort Collins to Colorado Springs, scheduled around field rotations. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite training at your facility, whether a Commerce City shop, a Weld County field office or a fabrication plant, using your instruments and representative specimens.
  • Blended delivery that runs theory online over several weeks and finishes with an onsite practical and exam block.

Scheduling on the Front Range follows the weather and the work. Winter storms can close roads to field locations; pipeline and facility construction peaks in the warmer months; refinery and power plant outages follow their own calendars. Many Colorado companies find late autumn and winter the best time to train, when field work slows and crews are available. Share your window and headcount for a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Denver crew, or see our corporate NDT training programme.

Where NDT technicians work in Denver

Oil and gas. The DJ Basin north and east of Denver supports production facilities, gathering systems, compressor stations and processing plants. Oil and gas development in Colorado is regulated by the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission (formerly the COGCC), while pipeline safety is overseen by PHMSA for interstate lines and the Colorado Public Utilities Commission gas pipeline safety programme for intrastate gas systems.

Refining. The Commerce City refinery is the state's refining anchor and a source of turnaround and mechanical-integrity work for UT, PAUT, RT, MT and VT technicians.

Power and utilities. Utility-owned generating stations in the Denver area and at Pueblo create outage work, and the ongoing transition from coal to gas and renewables brings new construction and fabrication inspection.

Aerospace and space. Denver is one of the largest space-industry centres in the US, with launch vehicle, spacecraft and satellite companies across Centennial, Littleton, Louisville, Boulder and Broomfield, and Buckley Space Force Base in Aurora. These employers generally qualify NDT personnel under NAS 410; Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 certification, though our PT, ET and UT courses build method knowledge.

Fabrication and infrastructure. Structural steel for Denver's construction market, CDOT bridges, water infrastructure and rail equipment all require VT, MT and UT, typically to AWS D1.1 and AWS bridge welding requirements.

Picking a lane on the Front Range. Because the energy and aerospace economies qualify people differently, the most useful decision a new Denver technician can make is which one to aim at first. If your goal is field work in the DJ Basin, at the Commerce City refinery or with a pipeline contractor, SNT-TC-1A in VT, MT and UT, followed by UT Level II and possibly RT, is the direct route, and it keeps you employable on construction, maintenance and turnaround work across Colorado, Wyoming, Utah and New Mexico. If your goal is a space or aerospace manufacturer, expect to be hired and then qualified by that employer under its own programme; strong PT, ET and UT method knowledge and a clean record of logged experience make that process shorter. Fabrication shops are a sensible middle path, because they hire entry-level VT and MT technicians year-round and give you the experience base to move in either direction later. Whichever lane you choose, keep your own copies of training certificates, exam results and experience logs. Employers change and projects end, and a well-kept personal file is what lets the next employer certify you quickly.

Industrial radiography in Colorado. Colorado is an NRC Agreement State. The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment radiation programme licenses radioactive materials and registers radiation-producing machines, and the state's radiation control regulations include specific requirements for industrial radiography operations and personnel. Your SNT-TC-1A RT certificate does not replace those requirements.

What Denver employers ask for. SNT-TC-1A Level II in the method, experience with the applicable code, field safety training, a clean driving record for rural field work, and, for RT, radiographer certification. Some supervisory roles add API inspector or CWI credentials; Atlantis does not offer those courses. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Denver NDT companies

Front Range inspection companies often grow fast during a drilling or construction upswing, adding methods and staff faster than their paperwork keeps up. We help with:

  • Written practice development covering every method you perform, including advanced UT.
  • Outside Level III exam administration and practical specimen control.
  • Record audits and recertification tracking.
  • ASNT Level III preparation for senior technicians.

A common Colorado problem is the multi-site programme: a company with a shop in the Denver metro, a field office in Weld County and crews working out of state, where each location has kept its own records in its own way. When a customer audits one site, the whole programme is exposed. We consolidate records under one written practice, confirm that every certified technician has current training, experience, exam and vision evidence on file, and set up a recertification calendar so nothing expires unnoticed during a busy field season. Where your own Level III has left or retired, we can act as the outside Level III named in the written practice until you have a replacement.

Book a Level III consultation for your Colorado programme.

Practise before the practical exam

Our Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It suits Denver trainees who spend long stretches in the field between sessions. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees Atlantis course content, written practices and examinations.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Denver

How do I get NDT certified in Denver?

Join an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete classroom training and logged experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass the vision test. The employer certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Colorado?

Yes, for classroom hours your written practice accepts. Practical training and exams must be hands-on, which we deliver onsite.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Weeks of classroom, months of experience. See our training requirements matrix and your written practice for the minimums.

Do I need a license for radiography in Colorado?

Yes. The employer must be licensed or registered with CDPHE, and radiographers must meet Colorado's industrial radiography requirements, separate from SNT-TC-1A.

What does NDT training cost in Denver?

It depends on method, level, group size and delivery format. We do not publish prices; quotes come back within one business day. Request a Denver training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Denver employers?

Energy, fabrication and infrastructure employers work to SNT-TC-1A. Aerospace employers typically qualify under NAS 410.

Do you have a training centre in Denver?

No. Training is online and onsite at your facility.

Can penetrant testing be done in Colorado winters?

Yes, but below the standard temperature range in the governing procedure you need a procedure qualified for that temperature. Our PT course covers this.

Which method should I learn first for DJ Basin work?

VT and UT thickness work are common starting points, followed by MT and PT, then UT Level II and RT.

Can you train our crew in Greeley or Pueblo?

Yes. Onsite delivery anywhere on the Front Range is standard.

Do you offer API or CWI training?

No. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Can you fix our written practice before an audit?

Yes. Our Level III reviews and updates it and your records.
